parts.title: A Summer in the Marsh
parts.text: Zaid, Hollis, and Emi spent the summer at a coastal nature center, helping Dr. Mbeki, a **conservationist** who protected rare birds. On the first morning she led them across a quiet **wetland** where reeds swayed over shallow water. "Marsh cranes are **vulnerable**," she told them. "Too few chicks survive, and if we fail them, the species could become **extinct**, gone forever like the dodo."

parts.title: Dangers Near and Far
parts.text: Emi learned that some people **poach** crane eggs and sell them illegally. Hollis pointed to the bulldozers beyond the fence, where a new housing project had begun to **encroach** on the edge of the marsh. "Every acre we lose could **endanger** more birds," Dr. Mbeki said. Inside the clinic, a crane with a bent wing rested on soft straw. The team would **rehabilitate** her, feeding her fish and exercising her wing. For now she was **captive**, but only until she was strong enough to fly.

parts.title: Back to the Sky
parts.text: In October, the healed crane was released at the **reserve**, a protected area where hunting was banned. Zaid fitted her with a tiny tracker so scientists could follow her and **safeguard** her route. Then the whole flock rose together and began its yearly **migration** south, their calls echoing across the water.

parts.title: What Hollis Understood
parts.text: Hollis wiped his eyes and laughed. Saving a species, he realized, did not take magic. It took patience, careful work, and people who refused to look away. The three friends promised to return next summer and to bring more volunteers with them.

definitions.meaning1: No longer existing; having died out completely. Example: Dinosaurs became extinct millions of years ago.
definitions.meaning2: No longer active, as a volcano that will not erupt again. Example: The village sits at the foot of an extinct volcano.

definitions.meaning2: To cook food gently in simmering liquid. Example: She learned to poach eggs in hot water.

definitions.meaning1: To help a sick, injured, or troubled person or animal return to good health or normal life. Example: Volunteers rehabilitate injured owls before setting them free.
definitions.meaning2: To restore something to good condition. Example: The city plans to rehabilitate the old theater.

definitions.meaning1: Easy to harm, attack, or hurt; lacking protection. Example: Newborn turtles are vulnerable to hungry gulls.

definitions.meaning1: A person who works to protect nature, wildlife, and natural resources. Example: The conservationist taught farmers how to protect rivers and forests.

definitions.meaning2: The movement of people from one place to live in another. Example: The migration of workers to the cities changed the country.
